newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS says Copenhagen-Stockholm traffic stable.
newsitem.headline: SAS says Copenhagen-Stockholm traffic stable.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Monday that its traffic on the key Copenhagen-Stockholm route was unchanged in May, despite new competition from Danish Maersk Air and Finland's Finnair.
"Our traffic on the route in May is comparable to that of the same month last year and I reckon that we took about 90 percent of the market," SAS executive Vagn Soerensen told Reuters.
"We are very satisfied, things have gone much better than expected," he said.
Maersk, owned by shipping group A.P. Moeller, was also pleased with initial results.
"Everything has gone exceedingly well, with traffic growing steadily throughout the first month of operation," sales executive Ejvin Pedersen said.

"In the fourth week of operation we achieved a 30 percent utilisation capacity, which is much better than we expected. It looks like we should achieve our aim of a 25 percent market share quicker than foreseen," he added.
He had no comment on the SAS statement.
Maersk launched regular Copenhagen-Stockholm flights on April 28, in cooperation with Finnair.
The route is one of the most lucrative and important for SAS, which has seen its dominant position in Scandinavian traffic challenged in recent months by other airlines.
Maersk Air/Finnair have eight flights per day between Copenhagen and Stockholm and around 30 percent of the route's total seat capacity, with SAS offering the remainder.

On May 6, SAS announced a 269 million Swedish crown pre-tax loss for the first quarter of 1997, attributing the disappointing result in part to competition. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33968653
